sampling_model.design: For fixed-law supporting results, regular samples jointly identify \(p\), \(r\), and \(\mu\). For the headline questions, row \(n\) contains independent observations from \(P_n^\circ\), with fixed finite supports, target \(\beta_n\), and context, action, and response-study identifying-cell probabilities bounded below by \(\kappa_n\).
sampling_model.units: Target contexts and actions are multinomial draws; separate interventional response units identify every finite \((c,x)\) cell. Dependence across the stacked components is allowed through a declared row influence vector.
sampling_model.treatment: The response study observes micro action \(X\); target macro action \(h\) uses an unknown context-only selector calibrated to \(r\).
sampling_model.overlap: The class \(\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}\) imposes only the floors on \(p_n\), \(r_n\), and \(\pi_n\), with \(\kappa_n\downarrow0\); it imposes no condition on \(n\kappa_n^3\) and no tuning condition. The sufficient question separately studies \(n\kappa_n^3\to\infty\), while the sharpness question separately fixes \(n\kappa_n\to\infty\) and bounded \(n\kappa_n^3\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The stacked estimator \(\widehat\beta_n\) obeys the assumed uniform bounded-Lipschitz row-Gaussian approximation, and its multiplier draw obeys the assumed conditional bounded-Lipschitz approximation uniformly over \(\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}\). The confidence procedure is indexed by an arbitrary deterministic schedule \(t=(t_n)\); the headline questions impose rate relations only within their own quantifiers.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Specified version-assignment laws identify overall multiple-version effects.
Section 2.1.1, Theorem 1, Equation (4), gives a constructive sharp identified set for partially linear coefficients from unlinked outcome and covariate margins.
Causal consistency requires intervention behavior to commute across related structural models.
Constructive causal abstractions relate low-level and high-level models through state and intervention maps.
Proposition 1 and Definition 6 give the all-intervention partial-projection condition, while Equation 11 fixes a canonical residual conditional law for a fixed low-level SCM and abstraction map.
The COTA objective is jointly convex in causally constrained transport plans.
Estimated measures and costs produce optimal-face transport limits.
Parametric optimization theory gives directional expansions of optimal values under nonunique solution and multiplier sets.
Danskin's envelope theorem expresses directional derivatives through the optimizing set.
The numerical delta method consistently estimates directionally differentiable limit laws with a slowly vanishing step.
Derivative-based resampling restores inference for directionally differentiable maps when the ordinary bootstrap fails.
The linear-program value procedure has a delta-conditioned uniform-consistency guarantee under optimizer multiplicity.
PDX precision strategies are compared with clinically meaningful controls under known recommendation rules.

Methodology, Theorem 3.2, gives uniformly valid confidence sets for linear functionals defined by linear moment inequalities by bootstrapping fixed, randomly perturbed linear-program value functions; coverage over the exact identified set tends to one and exact coverage is obtained on an outer perturbed set.

Main Results, Theorem 3, gives uniformly valid confidence sets for sharp scalar projections of finite affine identified sets under uniform positive rank, slack, and moment constants, allowing multiplicity of primal optima.

body.tldr: The sole headline frontier is procedure-specific: whether \(n\kappa_n^3\to\infty\), together with \((n\kappa_n)^{-1/2}=o(t_n)\) and \(t_n=o(\kappa_n)\), suffices for uniform simultaneous coverage by the row-feasible paired numerical-delta selector envelope, and whether every vanishing deterministic schedule fails on some \(2\times2\) array when \(n\kappa_n^3\) is bounded despite \(n\kappa_n\to\infty\). Cho--Russell and Gafarov already establish uniform LP inference by different perturbation or regularization procedures, so uniform LP inference itself is not claimed as new. The explicit projected SCM construction, sharp transport image, flow certificates, cycle additivity, fixed-interior sensitivity, and pointwise Hong--Li inference remain supporting infrastructure at incremental scope.

project_justification.gap: Cho--Russell give uniformly valid but deliberately conservative inference from fixed nonvanishing random LP perturbations, while Gafarov gives uniformly valid sharp affine-set projection inference under uniform positive rank and slack constants and allows flat primal faces. Those results do not settle the validity or sharp boundary of the row-feasible paired numerical-delta procedure when transport margins and response cells shrink.
project_justification.niche: The remaining field-level niche is a procedure-specific decay boundary with exact tuning quantifiers and an actual coverage-distortion sequence, not a claim that uniform inference for linear programs is new.
project_justification.fill: The project defines \(\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}\) independently of tuning, asks sufficiency under the only proposed rare-cell step window, and separately asks the for-every-schedule sharpness question. The two-branch \(2\times2\) handle distinguishes feasibility-correction distortion from optimal-face localization failure.

body.related_work: VanderWeele and Hernán show that multiple-version effects depend on a specified version-assignment distribution. Béal and Latouche apply that setup to PDX precision-medicine comparisons. D'Haultfoeuille, Gaillac, and Maurel, Section 2.1.1, Theorem 1 and Equation (4), characterize a sharp coefficient set under unlinked margins through transport; that result informs the discrete selector envelope. Rubenstein et al. and Beckers and Halpern inform the intervention and abstraction semantics. Xia and Bareinboim, Proposition 1 and Definition 6, supply the partial-projection condition instantiated by the semantic lemma; their Equation 11 canonical residual law is fixed and cannot span a positive-dimensional free-selector polytope. Felekis et al. inform the transport representation. Bonnans and Shapiro and Danskin directly supply the parametric linear-program sensitivity tools, while Hundrieser et al. study estimated-cost transport. Fang and Santos provide the general directional-inference framework, and Hong and Li supply the fixed-law numerical-delta corollary. Cho and Russell, Methodology, Theorem 3.2, obtain uniform inference for linear functionals defined by linear moment inequalities by bootstrapping randomly perturbed LP values. The selector interval embeds as one scalar partially identified functional, and their four lower and upper perturbed programs address both endpoints. Their stated class can accommodate finite rare-cell arrays under its boundedness and feasibility conditions, but their perturbation support is fixed and nonvanishing; coverage is one over the exact identified set and exact only on an outer perturbed set. Gafarov, Main Results, Theorem 3, constructs uniformly valid confidence sets for sharp affine identified-set projections, including flat primal faces, by regularized support functions. The selector envelope embeds in his finite affine system after one redundant margin equality is removed, but his uniform class fixes positive lower bounds on rank and no-overidentification slack; shrinking margins can leave that class, and his interval uses regularization and Bonferroni rather than the row-feasible paired numerical-delta critical value. Voronin provides delta-conditioned uniform consistency and pointwise inference for an LP-value procedure. These comparisons leave only the schedule-specific shrinking-margin boundary as the open novelty claim, with no assertion that uniform LP inference is new or that comparator assumptions are nested.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The selector seed \(S\) is atomless even though all endogenous and response domains are finite. The residual coordinate is endogenous with equation \(Z_s=g_s(C,S)\), which is essential for interventions on \(C\) to commute; its induced conditional law varies with \(s\). The result proves the Xia--Bareinboim Definition-6 partial-projection identity selector by selector and does not preserve one fixed canonical Equation-11 residual law or one common canonical Layer-3 map across distinct selectors.
body.honest_scope: The sufficient-regime and schedule-quantified procedural-sharpness questions jointly form the sole headline and remain open, conditional on the displayed uniform bounded-Lipschitz Gaussian and multiplier approximations. The experiment class \(\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}\) contains no rate or tuning restrictions. A failure theorem concerns only \(\mathrm{CI}_n(t)\) and would not imply minimax impossibility for other confidence procedures. Cho--Russell and Gafarov already provide uniform LP inference using different perturbation and regularization constructions. The projected SCM construction, sharp image and attainment, endpoint certificates, fixed-map obstruction, cycle criterion, fixed-interior derivative, and pointwise Hong--Li corollary are supporting theorem targets at incremental scope. No uniform theorem, failure theorem, comparator nesting, or fixed canonical Equation-11 map for the free-selector family is claimed.
